definitions.explanation: The first one in a sequence, or the starting point of something. Can function as a noun or adverbial expression.

examples.japanese: {最初|さいしょ}から{読|よ}んでください。
{最初|さいしょ}は{難|むずか}しかったです。
{最初|さいしょ}に{名前|なまえ}を{書|か}いてください。
examples.notes: 最初に = first, to begin with

examples.japanese: {最初|さいしょ}の{一歩|いっぽ}が{大切|たいせつ}です。
{日本|にほん}に{来|き}た{最初|さいしょ}の{日|ひ}は、{何|なに}も{分|わ}からなくて{大変|たいへん}でした。
examples.english: On my first day in Japan, I didn't understand anything and it was tough.

notes:
{最初|さいしょ} means "first" or "beginning" and can function as a noun or adverbially.

COMMON PATTERNS:
- {最初|さいしょ}に: first, at first (adverbial)
- {最初|さいしょ}から: from the beginning
- {最初|さいしょ}は: at first, initially
- {最初|さいしょ}の〜: the first ~ (attributive)

DISTINCTION:
- {最初|さいしょ}: the first (in sequence/time), beginning
- {初|はじ}めて: for the first time (first experience)
- {初|はじ}め: beginning (often in {初|はじ}めに)

CONTRAST:
Opposite of {最後|さいご} (last, end).

EXAMPLE USAGE:
{最初|さいしょ}は{難|むずか}しかったが、だんだん{慣|な}れた。
(It was difficult at first, but I gradually got used to it.)
